author: val
body: SourceDefWire had no behavioural test before this one. It was reached only by foreword-all-compile, which compiles it and asks it nothing. That is the gap the chapter's own opening paragraph exists to close: the format has two independent sides, written by apps RepoProtocolPersist and read by the compiler through foreword FactDisk, and a divergence between them is exactly what a crossing test is for.

author: val
body: The first two rows print the encoded line itself, so the expected file pins the wire bytes and not merely the symmetry. A round trip alone cannot express both sides being wrong the same way, which is the failure mode a shared codec is most prone to; an encoder and a decoder that agree with each other and with nothing else pass every round trip. The remaining rows then check that decode recovers what encode was given, with the content carrying a pipe, a newline, nothing at all, and a signature of every byte class including 0, 127, 128 and 255.

author: val
body: The three refuse rows and the two CONTROL rows are a pair and neither half means anything alone. Until 2026-07-28 sdw-encode did not enforce the rule the chapter states, so a pipe in a header field produced a line whose fields were all shifted by one and decode answered Just a record with eight of ten readings wrong, silently; only hash survived, being the field before the injected pipe. Encode now answers Maybe and refuses. The controls exist because refusing everything would pass a refusal-only test: content carrying pipes must still encode, since a pipe is how the language writes a sum type and the content is the field the format is built to let hold them.
